annotation.title_clean: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence
annotation.title_en: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence
annotation.authors_or_issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
annotation.summary_en: NIST Special Publication 1270 is voluntary guidance on identifying and managing bias in AI. It sets out three bias categories (systemic, statistical, human) and a socio-technical approach. It gives preliminary guidance on datasets, testing and evaluation (TEVV), human factors and governance, as a step toward formal standards and the NIST AI RMF.
key_provisions_or_claims: Identifies three categories of AI bias: systemic, statistical/computational, and human.
Advocates a socio-technical approach rather than computational-only bias mitigation.
Gives guidance on datasets, TEVV and human factors, including diversity and human-in-the-loop design.
Guidance is voluntary and does not supersede law; it is a first step toward formal NIST guidance and the AI RMF.
Notes that zero bias risk is not achievable and bias mitigation should align with legal standards.
